## The checker's report

Check of the design sheet of Princess Playground (`princess-playground`, band 2 to 5), round 7, checker I. Sheet part hash confirmed: 9c1057ba1c87d26f63b53754085317fd3f07c8f60f8130653a5cb384ce859cc7.

Records: all 13 looked up by id today. Code, standing and check state are as the sheet says: five us-ca department-published foundations and `us-ca K.MD.2` (state-board-adopted standard), seven nl curriculum-institute-guidance statements, every one `confirmed`.
Limits: every "Limits taken" line read against that record's Limits section; none says more than Limits, and no changed sentence touches a record, a limit or the claim.
Levels: not looked up again, since no changed text touches a level. The round 6 sheet part with the builder's 33 listed changes applied equals the round 7 sheet part exactly, so there is no unnamed change. The sweep for rulings 8, 9 and 11 found nothing: 30 grid cells each have a sound and no row or column shares one, parts are named beside each code and in the claim, and the claim says the game offers a character.

Findings

1. "The band and its age rule", line 13, "What follows for the hand", fourth and fifth sentences (change 5). The change drops "well apart", which the guide's "By age" asks of essential targets for ages 2 to 4 (pack: game-design, ages-2-to-4.md), and now allows touching pictures everywhere, including where the game itself lays the friends out. Replace the two sentences with:
`Each friend is a target of about 100 logical pixels or more, and none stands in the bottom strip where wrists rest. Where the game sets the friends down for a ride they stand well apart. Where the child has stacked them or set them down close their pictures may touch; a finger on a friend's body always takes that friend.`

2. "The scenes", line 143, "The ride", second sentence (follows from change 19). Line 85 now ends a ride when the asker is carried by the plank or set there by the child's hand, but the ending scene, "the ending of every cycle", still names only the plank as its cause, so a ride ended by hand has no stated ending. Replace `Cause: the plank carries the asker where it wanted to go.` with:
`Cause: the asker is where it wanted to go, carried there by the plank or set there by the child's hand.`

3. "The scenes", line 163, "How a ride ends and the next begins", last sentence (change 32). Ruling 12, near case: a showing put away before it starts does not play on load and is still owed; the sheet has it play by itself when the game is opened, which also goes against the same paragraph's "the ending does not play by itself" and line 153's rule that an unbegun showing waits for the next time its kind is laid out. Replace `A showing that was due and had not begun plays when the game is opened, as the very first one does.` with:
`A showing that was due and had not begun when the game was put away does not play by itself when the game is opened: the ride is found laid out, as it was saved when it began, and the showing is still owed and plays the next time a ride of that kind is laid out.`

4. "Where the two differ", line 218, "How many objects", second and third sentences (unchanged text, ruling 10 sweep). "The Dutch cards set no number" speaks for the cards as a whole, which the sheet does not say it read; only the Limits of `nl Gewicht / 4` say that no number of objects is set. Replace `The Dutch cards set no number. The game follows the Dutch cards, which leave the number open: a stack is the game's own choice.` with:
`The Dutch statement named here for comparing, `nl Gewicht / 4`, sets no number of objects. The game follows that statement, which leaves the number open: a stack is the game's own choice.`

Checked and not findings:
- The arithmetic of the new grid paragraph holds. The only equal splits are Mog against Dot and Pim with Bo against Mog with Dot. The end that is down always holds someone. Pim can tip only an empty plank.
- Bo on a high end he cannot tip has no "If not" in his cell; his own answer is in the characters table (the chuckle that shakes the plank), so "answers in its own way" leaves him a motion and a sound.
- The ride found ended on load (change 32, first new sentence) gives the outcome ruling 12 asks for and can be rebuilt from the saved fields.
- `touched` is listed as a field and carries the rake's "from the first touch on" across loads (ruling 5).
- The asker's three hops are 1 + 2 = 3, back off and stop.
